notes:
The first clean single-version run: plugin 0.45.0 throughout, Claude Code 2.1.251, no session limit, no edits to the working tree while it ran.

It found two defects in the harness's own probes rather than in the organization, which is why it is kept.

`background-execution-was-actually-dispatched` reports not-run on job 9290e0bc for state `working`, while the same record says `produced: true`. The job ran and wrote its artifact; the poll caught it before it finished. The probe lumped every state other than `done` into 'the platform never ran it', and a state cannot turn work that demonstrably happened into work that did not. Corrected after this run: produced work passes whatever the job's state, a finished job that produced nothing fails, and only an unstarted or undetermined job is not-run.

`worktree-work-was-integrated-not-just-isolated` reports fail, and the failure is real -- three worktrees were created and none was removed. But its integration evidence was wrong: it accepted `src/retention/policy.py is modified in the main checkout`, which is exactly the trace an agent leaves when it ignores the worktree and edits the main checkout directly. The repository confirms it: one commit, the shipped baseline, and a dirty working tree. Had a removal been recorded, this probe would have passed on evidence of the opposite behaviour. Integration now requires a commit carrying the work out of the worktree.

Worktree creation is genuinely exercised here for the first time in a clean run: three created, WorktreeCreate fired for each. Removal and integration are still unproven, and REQ still escalates after three refusals.

Left as produced. A record is not rewritten to agree with a probe rule that came after it; the verdict stands and this note says what a re-run would show.

CORRECTION, 2026-09-04. Any `worktree-isolation-was-actually-used` pass in this record is FALSE. The probe counted `worktree_created` events, and those events fired whether or not a worktree existed: WorktreeCreate is a provider hook, so this plugin's recorder was replacing the platform's creation with a script that recorded an event and made nothing. Every such event carries `path: null`. Proven by controlled experiment -- removing the registration and changing nothing else produced a real worktree. The probe now reads `git worktree list`. The verdict in this file stands as produced; certification was refused in every one of these runs regardless, so no verdict changes.
